source.title: Resolving superposition in AI for interpretability and cross-modal alignment in patient-neuronal images
source.authors: Jisung Park; Seohyeon Kang; D. Yoo; Eunsu Lee; Seoin Cho; Wooyeop Choi; Янлим Чой; J. Evan; Daesoo Kim; Sonia Gandhi; Minee L. Choi

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates overlap between feature directions and changes in representation geometry using SAE dictionary-size and sparsity sweeps in biological CNNs, rather than reproducing the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own measurements of decoder-vector inner products, effective rank, and class-specific feature-map counts. Other biological analyses and cited findings are not included as rows because they do not directly measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study assumes the CNN superposes features because of a dimensional bottleneck. It then uses gated SAEs as a tool and reports only the SAEs' own properties against each other and against the CNN. These are decoder-column inner products, eRank, alive features, class-specific feature-map counts and downstream cell-death/kNN/Moran's I fidelity. None of these measures whether the CNN stores more sparse features than dimensions as overlapping directions, or whether its polysemanticity comes from capacity pressure. The 'CNN Proxy' is itself a 600-d SAE (λ=50), not the CNN. No toy model is used and no LLM is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors argue, from a generalized Welch bound and from SAE comparisons, that bottleneck superposition contaminates latent metric geometry and that SAEs restore it. They further conclude that SAE latents can be analysed with scRNA-seq tools and aligned with scRNA-seq via GW-map. Superposition in the CNN is assumed, not independently demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a contrastively trained biological-image CNN and gated SAEs, then evaluates decoder-vector inner products, effective rank, feature maps, and downstream geometry; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with SAE dictionary size and sparsity penalty; inner product increases at dictionary dimension 8192 relative to 4096 under fixed λ.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs trained on a biological-image CNN (stage5_out, 512-d) yield feature maps the authors describe as monosemantic, e.g. nuclear envelope, mitochondria. CNN maps co-activate for mitochondria and lysosomes (Fig. 4a, qualitative; Fig. 4b counts 697 vs 40 class-specific maps).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Indirect evidence in vision CNNs (non-LLM): SAEs recover sparse interpretable features from polysemantic CNN channels.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger, sparser SAE dictionaries give lower decoder-column overlap and higher eRank. SAE latents give better kNN cell-death coherence, Moran's I and ridge R2 than CNN features (Table 1, Figs 3, 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE expansion of a bottlenecked representation improves downstream metric/geometric fidelity (a representation-quality claim, not superposition itself).

record.problems: The empirical study uses a biological-image CNN setting and does not test toy networks or LLMs. Exact eRank values are only shown in a figure. The results do not test importance-based allocation of dedicated dimensions or establish stable, complete, canonical SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct measurements of the claim versions were left out. Downstream cell-death, transcriptomic-alignment, and pathway results were omitted because they do not directly measure feature overlap, capacity allocation, or one-dimensional feature geometry.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, no sparsity-driven phase transition, no geometry of the model's own feature directions; superposition in the CNN is assumed.
All: capacity pressure is assumed (Welch-bound argument), not tested; no importance manipulation or dedicated-dimension allocation.
All: no test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
All: no LLMs; SAE use on a vision CNN is a tool application.
All: no tests of SAE feature completeness, stability across runs or canonicity.
All: no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1/V2 support labels are rejected. All quantitative superposition-related numbers describe the SAE dictionaries (decoder inner products, eRank, feature counts), compared across SAE settings and with the CNN. That is method performance, the T4 case. The 'CNN Proxy' is an SAE, not the CNN. r7 duplicates r4. The V2 limits_scope label for an untested part was also misapplied. Downstream biology (cell death, GW-map) was rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use toy networks, establish a transition threshold as feature sparsity changes, or test regular geometries such as the toy-model configurations. Its empirical comparisons concern CNN representations and SAE dictionaries.

The study tests whether increased SAE dictionary capacity and sparsity relate to less overlap and more separable feature maps. It does not test whether feature importance determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
The models are biological-image CNNs, not LLMs; no LLM feature spreading or SAE recovery is assessed.
The paper evaluates SAE interpretability and geometric fidelity, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable across runs, or canonical units.
The paper measures inner products between decoder vectors but does not compare one-dimensional features with multi-dimensional features.

rows.subject: CNN Proxy
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product of concept vectors in the low-dimensional, low-sparsity SAE proxy for the CNN.
rows.note: The paper uses this as its baseline proxy; the value alone does not establish a result against a separately stated reference.
rows.check: Subject is a low-sparsity 600-d SAE trained as a stand-in, not the CNN. Its decoder inner product (0.160) describes that SAE's dictionary, not CNN feature geometry. It is a method-comparison reference, not a measurement of superposition.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product of concept vectors in the dictionary-size and sparsity sweep.
rows.note: The reported mean inner product is lower than the CNN Proxy reference.
rows.check: Mean inner product of SAE decoder columns compares SAE configurations with each other. This is the study's own method compared across settings. It does not measure overlap of features inside the CNN or toy-model geometry.

rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product of concept vectors in the dictionary-size and sparsity sweep.
rows.note: The reported mean inner product is lower than the CNN Proxy reference.
rows.check: Same as r2: an SAE dictionary property used for method comparison, not evidence on any version.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product of concept vectors in the dictionary-size and sparsity sweep.
rows.note: The reported value remains below the CNN Proxy reference, but increases from 0.082 at dictionary dimension 4096.
rows.check: Same as r2. Inner product rises from 0.082 (d=4096) to 0.104 (d=8192), a non-monotonic SAE behaviour, not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product while varying the sparsity penalty.
rows.note: The reported mean inner product is lower than the CNN Proxy reference.
rows.check: Sparsity-penalty sweep of SAE decoder inner products. This is method tuning, not a sparsity-dependent transition in the model's features.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product while varying the sparsity penalty.
rows.note: The reported mean inner product is lower than the CNN Proxy reference.
rows.check: Duplicate of r4 (d=4096, λ=800, 0.082). It is an SAE method comparison.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean inner product while varying the sparsity penalty.
rows.note: The reported mean inner product is lower than the CNN Proxy reference and than the values at λ = 200 and λ = 800.
rows.check: Same as r6. A higher SAE λ gives lower decoder overlap (0.052), which is a property of the SAE.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors
rows.operation_detail: Compared effective rank across dictionary sizes.

conditions.value: raw latent vectors, PCA projections, and PCA on standardized features

rows.note: The text states that eRank consistently increases from the CNN baseline as dictionary size scales under fixed λ across the three representation views; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: eRank of SAE latents rises with SAE dictionary size versus the 512-d CNN. A larger representation having higher effective rank does not show the CNN superposes features, and values are figure-only.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Counted mutation-specific feature maps using differential activation.

conditions.value: control to three PD mutation groups

rows.note: The paper reports the CNN total alongside the SAE total as a feature-map comparison.
rows.check: CNN count of mutation-specific feature maps (40) is a comparator for the study's SAE method. It is a differential-activation count, not a measure of polysemanticity or capacity.

rows.subject: Gated SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on CNN stage5_out spatial feature vectors; λ = 3200 for interpretability analyses
rows.operation_detail: Counted mutation-specific feature maps using differential activation.

conditions.value: control to three PD mutation groups

rows.note: The authors state that the SAE yields significantly more class-specific feature maps than the CNN baseline.
rows.check: The SAE-versus-CNN class-specific map count (697 vs 40) compares the study's method with its baseline. Dictionary size is not stated in the text; only λ=3200 is given. It does not test capacity allocation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Across the reported SAE settings, mean inner products are below the CNN Proxy value, and eRank rises with dictionary size; see r2–r9.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The mean inner product rises from 0.082 at dimension 4096 to 0.104 at dimension 8192, so overlap does not decline monotonically with dictionary size; see r4–r5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Biological CNN representations compared with expanded SAE features
reader_labels.reason: The SAE sweep reports lower mean inner products than the CNN Proxy, increasing eRank with dictionary size, and more mutation-specific feature maps; see r2–r11.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Feature importance and allocation of dedicated dimensions
reader_labels.reason: The study does not measure whether more important features receive dedicated dimensions while less important features share them; this part of V2 is untested rather than contradicted.
